Summary: The Exodus is Israel's deliverance from slavery in Egypt through the Red Sea under Moses, the defining Old Testament picture of redemption. Through plagues, Passover, and the covenant at Sinai, God showed He keeps His promises and dwells with His people. The New Testament reads the Exodus as a foreshadowing of the greater deliverance Jesus brings from sin.
KeyPassages: Exodus 3:7-10; Exodus 12:13; Exodus 14:13-14; Exodus 20:2; Deuteronomy 7:8; 1 Corinthians 10:1-4
RelatedQuestions: Did the Exodus really happen?; How does the Exodus point to Jesus?
